newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sony to launch DVD player in March.
newsitem.headline: Sony to launch DVD player in March.

text.p: Sony Corp said on Thursday that it would launch commercial sales of its digital video disc (DVD) player in March in Japan and that it would start sample deliveries of its DVD-ROM drive later this month.
The DVD player will be launched in the United States in April and in Europe in the middle of 1997, the Sony spokeswoman said.
The commercial launch of the DVD-ROM drive in Japan will be in the spring, a Sony spokeswoman said.

The DVD player, called the DVP-S7000, will be launched in Japan on March 21 and will be priced at 110,000 yen, Sony said in a statement. The player can play back DVD video software as well as music and video compact discs, it said.
Initial production is planned at a monthly rate of 5,000 units, the statement said.
The DVD player will be launched in the rest of Asia some time after its introduction to the U.S. market, she said without elaborating.
Samples of the DVD-ROM drive will be offered at 100,000 yen, the Sony statement said.
The spokeswoman said sample deliveries of the DVD-ROM drive would also start in January in the United States with commercial sales set to begin there in April.
Sony will also start selling a Dolby digital processor and an AV amplifier, priced at 88,000 yen each, in Japan on February 10, the statement said.
They are used with a DVD player or large-screen television set to enhance images and sounds, it said. They will be introduced in the United States in March, the Sony spokesman said.
The DVD system is expected to eventually replace video movies, compact discs (CDs) and CD-ROMs. A DVD looks like a CD, but can hold seven to 14 times as much data.
